I farm 10.1 mu here in Quzhou, wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone around me. I have been doing this 35 years, so I do not change much. What worked last year I do again.

For my wheat, I plow once with the small tractor after maize comes off in October, then sow. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — the kind everybody here plants, about 30 jin per mu so the stand is thick. Before sowing I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 kind, 50 jin each bag) on each mu as bottom fertilizer. Then when the wheat turns green in spring I throw down about 40 jin of urea per mu before the irrigation water comes. I water 3 times — one before winter so roots don't freeze dry, one at returning-green, one at heading when the ear is filling. I spray once against aphids in May, sometimes twice if I see many. Good year I get about 450 kg per mu, my neighbor Old Wang got 480 last year but his land is a bit better.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in June I do not plow, I just plant directly into the stubble with the seeder — saves time and diesel, everyone does this now. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shop is pushing that year, one bag does my whole field. I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer as starter when seeding, then about 50 jin urea per mu at big-trumpet stage before I water. I water once or twice depending on rain, usually once is enough because July-August rain here is good. Spray once for corn borer. Maize gives me more, maybe 550 kg per mu.

I don't have money to waste but I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose yield — a bad harvest costs much more than one extra bag.
